question: An HR project built eighteen months ago is still in daily use. Its benefits summary has since been superseded by a newer edition, and one uploaded policy was retired outright in a restructure. Which two actions should the project owner take? Select two.
options: A) Remove the retired policy, because an obsolete document still gets used in answers.
B) Ask Claude which uploaded documents are out of date and act on whatever it reports.
C) Upload the current benefits summary and delete the superseded edition it replaces.
D) Add an instruction telling Claude to disregard any document older than twelve months.
E) Keep both benefits editions in place so Claude can compare the old and new wording.
correct_answers: A) Remove the retired policy, because an obsolete document still gets used in answers.
C) Upload the current benefits summary and delete the superseded edition it replaces.
explanations: Correct, and this is a different maintenance action on a different document: nothing replaces the retired policy, so it is removed rather than refreshed. Claude has no way to know a policy no longer applies unless it stops being available.

Claude can compare documents it has been given, but it cannot know which reflects current company reality. Delegating the currency judgment to the model is precisely the human review step that project maintenance requires.

Correct. Refreshing the document is the fix for a superseded source, and deleting the old edition matters as much as adding the new one — left in place, it competes with the current figures and produces confidently wrong answers.

Uploaded files do not carry a reliable age Claude can filter on, and the rule would be wrong in both directions — discarding accurate long-standing policies while keeping a recently uploaded document that is already superseded.

Two live editions of the same summary is the situation that causes staff to be quoted last year's benefits. If a historical version is genuinely needed, it belongs outside the project knowledge that answers everyday questions.
